name: Anterior cruciate ligament
description: From the lateral wall of the intercondylar notch to the anterior intercondylar tibia, in anteromedial and posterolateral bundles. Low to intermediate and striated, roughly parallel to the Blumensaat line in extension; best on sagittal images.

normal_values.acl_tibial_plateau_angle: 45° or more; below 45° supports a tear
normal_values.acl_blumensaat_angle: about 0° or negative (ACL steeper than the roof); tear cutoffs range from above 0° to above 15°
normal_values.anterior_tibial_translation: 5 mm or less at the mid lateral condyle; above 5–7 mm supports a tear

variants_pitfalls: Striated, intermediate signal is normal: judge fiber continuity and course, not brightness.
Mucoid degeneration (about 1–14%): thickened, with intact fibers on T2, a normal course and often footprint cysts. A ganglion (about 1%) is a discrete fluid mass splaying intact fibers.

Torn but intact-looking: about 30% of chronic complete tears leave a scar band, and the infrapatellar plica lies just in front. A band flatter than the Blumensaat line or not anchored on the lateral notch wall is not a normal ACL; check coronal and axial images.
Secondary signs (pivot-shift contusions, anterior translation, PCL buckling, a lateral notch deeper than 1.5 mm) are specific but insensitive; their absence does not clear the ACL.
